newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen steady, property may firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen steady, property may firm.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was seen steady on Wednesday with recently battered property counters likely to rebound after the government denied late on Tuesday having any plans to hold a news briefing this week.
"The property market failed to react much yesterday because people were trying to assimilate the news. But I think they should rebound today," said an institutional broker.
The market had been rife with talk of more restrictive measures on the property sector.
Shares could also be boosted by Wall Street's strong performance overnigt.
However, dealers warned market upside might be limited as foreign investors continued to shy away from the region, preferring other areas like the U.S. and Latin America.
They said while it was uncertain if the market has hit its bottom, there were good values for picking now.
Some of the stocks recommended were property counters like DBS Land, SingLand, Wing Tai, and foreign tranches of banks like UOB and DBS, as well as selected electronic stocks.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 6.59 points down on Tuesday at 1,990.20. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
